_meta.indication: VIZIMPRO is indicated for the first-line treatment of patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations as detected by an FDA-approved test.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, multinational, open-label study; patients randomized 1:1 to VIZIMPRO 45 mg orally once daily or gefitinib 250 mg orally once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with unresectable, metastatic NSCLC with no prior therapy for metastatic disease, ECOG performance status 0 or 1, and EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) as determined by blinded Independent Radiologic Central (IRC) review per RECIST v1.1.
pivotal_trials.n: A total of 452 patients randomized to VIZIMPRO (N=227) or gefitinib (N=225).
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 14.7 months (VIZIMPRO) vs 9.2 months (gefitinib); HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.47, 0.74); p<0.0001. ORR 75% vs 72% (p=0.39).

key_safety: Most common (>20%) adverse reactions were diarrhea (87%), rash (69%), paronychia (64%), stomatitis (45%), decreased appetite (31%), dry skin (30%), decreased weight (26%), alopecia (23%), cough (21%), and pruritus (21%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 27% of patients; most common serious reactions were diarrhea (2.2%) and interstitial lung disease (1.3%).
target_moa: Dacomitinib is an ATP-competitive, irreversible small molecule pan-HER (EGFR/HER1, HER2, HER4) tyrosine kinase inhibitor, with activity against wild-type EGFR and the exon 19 deletion and exon 21 L858R mutant EGFR.

rems.type: The clinical review determined that risk mitigation and evaluation strategies under FDAAA are not necessary; a REMS was not required for this application.

companion_dx_detail: The QIAGEN therascreen EGFR RGQ PCR Kit was approved as a companion diagnostic for the detection of EGFR exon 19 deletions and exon 21 L858R mutations to identify patients with NSCLC for VIZIMPRO.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was requested for this application.

orphan_indication.text: Dacomitinib was granted orphan drug designation on March 3, 2015, for the treatment of NSCLC with EGFR, HER2, HER4, or DDR2 mutations.

summary.text: VIZIMPRO received regular (full) approval as a new molecular entity under a Priority review, supported by ARCHER 1050. It had received orphan drug designation on March 3, 2015 for NSCLC with EGFR/HER2/HER4/DDR2 mutations. The reviewers concluded the evidence met the statutory standard for regular approval.

citations.quote: In the opinion of the reviewers, the submitted evidence meets the statutory evidentiary standard for regular approval. The magnitude of the treatment effect on PFS in ARCHER 1050 is large and clinically meaningful and is consistent with a significant improvement in the treatment of an advanced NSCLC population with unmet medical need.
